sections.title: Types of crime
sections.content:
Vocabulary for discussing criminal offences:
• fraud — deception for financial gain. He was convicted of tax fraud.
• bribery — offering money to influence someone's actions. Bribery of public officials carries heavy penalties.
• embezzlement — stealing money entrusted to your care. The accountant was charged with embezzlement of company funds.
• vandalism — deliberate destruction of property. Vandalism in the park cost the city thousands to repair.
• cybercrime — criminal activity using computers. Cybercrime costs businesses billions every year.

sections.title: Legal process
sections.content:
Key terms in the justice system:
• verdict — the decision of a jury. The jury delivered a guilty verdict after three days.
• acquit — to find not guilty. The defendant was acquitted due to lack of evidence.
• prosecute — to bring legal action against someone. The state decided to prosecute the company for pollution.
• sentence — the punishment given by a court. He received a five-year prison sentence.
• bail — money paid to release someone before trial. The judge set bail at fifty thousand dollars.

sections.title: Law enforcement
sections.content:
People and actions in maintaining order:
• detective — an officer who investigates crimes. The detective solved the case using forensic evidence.
• witness — a person who sees an event. Three witnesses testified in court.
• surveillance — close monitoring of a person or place. The suspect was under surveillance for six months.
• forensic — relating to scientific methods of solving crimes. Forensic analysis of the DNA confirmed the suspect's identity.

exercises.question: Deceiving someone for financial gain is:
exercises.hint: A form of dishonesty involving money.
exercises.explanation: Fraud is wrongful deception intended for personal or financial gain.

exercises.question: When a jury finds a defendant not guilty, they:
exercises.explanation: To acquit means to free someone from a criminal charge by a verdict of not guilty.

exercises.question: Stealing money that was placed in your care is:
exercises.hint: Often committed by accountants or managers.
exercises.explanation: Embezzlement is theft of funds placed in one's trust.

exercises.question: The punishment given by a court after a guilty verdict is a:
exercises.hint: It could be prison time or a fine.
exercises.explanation: A sentence is the punishment assigned to a defendant found guilty.

exercises.question: Offering money to influence someone in a position of power is:
exercises.hint: An illegal payment to gain advantage.
exercises.explanation: Bribery is the act of offering something valuable to influence the actions of an official.

exercises.question: Scientific methods used to investigate crime are called:
exercises.explanation: Forensic relates to the application of scientific knowledge to legal problems.

exercises.question: Money paid to release an accused person before their trial is:
exercises.explanation: Bail is money paid to a court to allow a person's temporary release while awaiting trial.

exercises.question: Close observation of a suspected criminal by authorities is:
exercises.explanation: Surveillance is close observation, especially of a suspected person.
